note: Discovery leads for nursing/allied-health topic workers (phase 4). LITERACY level: teach what each concept IS and why it matters, with original examples. HEALTH-SCIENCE CONTENT — accuracy is paramount: Tier A sources for every clinical claim; no invented numbers; every definition attributed. The biology subject owns organ-system physiology; anatomy-depth and biochemistry belong to biology — nursing lessons teach the professional practice level.

tierA.useFor: textbook backbone — nursing skills (vital signs, assessment, documentation), pharmacology foundations, medical terminology. openstax.org may block direct fetch — try live first, else Wayback captures with canonical URLs. REFERENCE_ONLY (CC BY-NC-SA: no source wording reproduced; aiIngestionAllowed false)

infection control (chain of infection, hand hygiene, standard/transmission-based precautions — the HICPAC/CDC guidelines), vaccines. cdc.gov blocks direct fetch — use archive.cdc.gov / web.archive.org captures
patient safety (WHO Patient Safety), hand hygiene (WHO 5 Moments), healthcare worker safety
consumer-level clinical facts (vital signs ranges, medications, confidentiality)
research literacy, evidence-based practice, clinical trials basics (NLM/NIH)

tierA.provider: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ)
tierA.useFor: patient safety, falls prevention, communication in healthcare, teamwork
HIPAA privacy rule (confidentiality, U.S. legal floor stated simply)
clinical judgment model, delegation, scope of practice (Tier A/B)

tierB.useFor: ethics (Code of Ethics), nursing process, scope and standards
patient safety goals, communication standards (Tier A/B)
clinical reference corroboration (vital signs, assessment techniques)

cautions: VITAL SIGN RANGES: use attributed adult reference ranges (e.g., temperature ~97-99F/36.1-37.2C, pulse 60-100, respirations 12-20, BP <120/80, SpO2 95-100% room air) with the source named; ranges vary by age — state adult context; NO invented precision.

CLINICAL SAFETY: no dosing advice anywhere; pharmacology teaches concepts (pharmacokinetics phases, medication rights), never doses. Medication-safety lesson teaches the 'rights' and the double-check culture — factual.

INFECTION CONTROL: chain of infection (agent, reservoir, portal of exit, mode of transmission, portal of entry, susceptible host), standard precautions (hand hygiene, PPE, safe injection), transmission-based (contact/droplet/airborne) — all CDC-attributed.

LEGAL/ETHICS: HIPAA confidentiality stated simply as the U.S. legal floor (no legal advice); ethics lesson teaches the ANA Code themes and principlism (autonomy, beneficence, nonmaleficence, justice) — the philosophy subject owns theory depth (reference only).
INFORMED CONSENT: teach the elements (capacity, information, voluntariness) and the nurse's role vs the provider's duty — factual, no legal advice.
DOCUMENTATION: charting principles (accurate, timely, complete, objective) and the 'if it wasn't documented, it wasn't done' culture — factual.
SCOPE: biology owns anatomy/physiology/biochemistry depth; psychology owns therapeutic-communication theory; only reference siblings.

Distribute question answer keys EVENLY across A/B/C/D (≥1 C, ≥1 D per topic; max 3 of 5 per slot). Verify keys from the file yourself. BANNED: 'Which statement best defines X used in this lesson?' stems — write scenario questions.
